claims.text: A mid-size SaaS company (about 400 people) rolled out an internal copilot over its Confluence space, and within three weeks a support engineer asking how to rotate a customer API key was given the procedure from a superseded 2022 runbook.
claims.how_to_use: Opener. This is the piece's scene; start inside it.

claims.text: The superseded runbook was never deleted or marked stale, and its title was nearly identical to the current page's.
claims.how_to_use: Immediately after C1. The mechanism of the failure.

claims.text: An audit of roughly 1,100 pages in the indexed space found about a third untouched for more than two years, roughly 140 with a near-duplicate carrying conflicting instructions, and roughly 60 whose listed owner no longer worked at the company.
claims.how_to_use: Proof section. Present as approximate figures from the writer's own audit, not as industry statistics.

claims.text: AI readiness assessments inventory models, vendors, and use cases, and almost never inventory the document corpus the model will retrieve from.
claims.how_to_use: The turn from the anecdote to the argument. Writer's view, stated as such.

claims.text: When a readiness deck does mention data quality, it means structured data in the warehouse, not the wiki.

The quiet discount is the invisible filtering a human reader applies to a stale page (the date in the breadcrumb, the departed author, the slightly wrong product name) that a retrieval system cannot apply, so documentation good enough for a reader is not automatically good enough for a retriever.
claims.how_to_use: The piece's apparatus. Name it, define it once, then use it to explain C1 and to motivate C8.

claims.text: A retriever ranking two near-identical chunks has no context beyond the text, so it can return the superseded one with full confidence.
claims.how_to_use: Mechanism under C6. Keep it at the level of what the writer observed; do not explain embeddings or ranking internals (non-goal).

claims.text: Before a copilot indexes a space, run three checks: pages with no current owner, pages with a near-duplicate, and pages nobody has opened in a year; then fix or archive what the checks surface.
claims.how_to_use: The close. This is what changes for the reader.

claims.text: The three-check audit is a few days of unglamorous work and would have prevented the key rotation incident.
claims.how_to_use: Last paragraph, to set expectations about effort.

claims.text: Most enterprise copilot deployments fail within the first year because of content quality.
claims.how_to_use: Do not use. Captured because the raw notes gesture at it; the writer has no source and web search was off. Listed so the writer sees the claim they wanted and cannot yet make.

gaps: Confirm whether the audit figures in C3 can be printed as given or need further rounding; the draft will present them as approximate either way.
Supply one sentence on what the client did after the audit (archived N pages? assigned owners?) if it can be shared; the close is stronger with an outcome.
If you want C10 in the piece, find a primary source; otherwise it stays out.
